issue.title: 3.4: Remove unused crypto and the SW geo-queue twin

affected_files.role: Verified: contains hashFacebookID (line 12), generateSalt (line 36), hashWithSalt (line 53). Grep across the entire repo shows hashFacebookID is referenced ONLY by its own tests/unit/crypto.test.js (8 matches) and its own definition. No production import. Per the issue, either wire it into the service worker (it hashes Facebook c_user cookie values per the PRD) or delete it together with its tests.

Verified: 293 lines, exports queueGeolocationLookup, getGeolocationForDomain, getQueueStats, clearRateLimitHistory, clearPendingQueue. The dashboard has its own geolocation client (src/dashboard/utils/geolocation.js) with the same exports. service-worker.js has the import commented out (line 18). Only the tests/unit/geo-queue.test.js file imports from this module. Per #19 (closed), cleartext ip-api.com lookups were halted and the live fetcher is now opt-in. The SW has no use for this file — the dashboard handles all geolocation. Per the issue, delete this file plus its test.

analysis.summary: F-DEAD-001/002/003, F-SEC-002: three concrete dead-code findings. (1) src/lib/crypto.js's hashFacebookID has zero production callers — only its own tests touch it. (2) src/lib/geo-queue.js is the SW twin of src/dashboard/utils/geolocation.js, and it has zero production callers (service-worker.js has it commented out; the dashboard never imports it). (3) DEBUG_MODE = true in geo-queue.js goes away with the file. (4) generateSalt and hashWithSalt are also dead in production (same reasoning). All three findings close with a single deletion PR. The alternative — wire hashFacebookID into the service worker to hash the c_user cookie — is not warranted by the PRD: the PRD says hashing is for cross-session identification, but no such use exists in code today, and adding one expands the privacy surface for a benefit not on the P3 roadmap.
analysis.details: Verification: ripgrep across the entire repo (excluding node_modules) shows hashFacebookID referenced only in src/lib/crypto.js and tests/unit/crypto.test.js. No production import. queueGeolocationLookup is exported from both geo-queue.js and geolocation.js, but the only import of the SW version is tests/unit/geo-queue.test.js (the SW service-worker.js has the import commented out at line 18). The dashboard version (geolocation.js) is used by SettingsSheet (getGeoOptIn/setGeoOptIn) and MapView (via the geolocation helpers). The survivor is geolocation.js. Per the issue, 'delete or wire hashFacebookID' and 'delete geo-queue.js or the dashboard duplicate — keep one geo client'. The simplest path is delete + delete, which also drops two test files. Verification per the issue body: `rg -n "hashFacebookID|geo-queue" src tests` should return no matches (with --include '*.{js,jsx}' or similar). The bug label is appropriate because the dead code also implicates F-SEC-002: a SHA-256 hasher of Facebook IDs that is not used is a stale attack surface (a future wire-up would not be reviewed).

options.name: Delete src/lib/crypto.js, src/lib/geo-queue.js, and their test files
options.summary: rm the two production files and their two test files. Remove the commented import in service-worker.js. Result: hashFacebookID, generateSalt, hashWithSalt, and the entire SW geo twin are gone. The dashboard geolocation client (src/dashboard/utils/geolocation.js) is the sole geo client. Verification command `rg -n "hashFacebookID|geo-queue" src tests` returns nothing.

files_to_modify.changes: remove the commented import of geo-queue.js

pros: Smallest diff, closes all three DEAD findings and F-SEC-002
Removes a stale attack surface (the unwired hasher)
Reduces the test surface and the bundle weight
cons: If a future task wants the c_user hashing, the code must be re-introduced (low cost)
options.risk_details: Pure deletion. Risks: (1) the commented import in service-worker.js is the only DOM-touching change. (2) Verify no other path imports the deleted modules — grep confirms not. (3) vitest.config.js may reference the deleted test files; check coverage include/exclude patterns.

options.name: Wire hashFacebookID into the service worker, then delete geo-queue.js
options.summary: Hash the c_user cookie value with hashFacebookID when the content script delivers a detection from facebook.com, store the hash as a non-PII identifier, and write the test fixture for the new path. Still delete src/lib/geo-queue.js because it has no caller. Larger PR; introduces a new behavior.

decision_record.root_cause: F-DEAD-001/002/003 + F-SEC-002: hashFacebookID has no production caller, src/lib/geo-queue.js has no production caller, and DEBUG_MODE = true in geo-queue.js is dead. The dead SHA-256 hasher of Facebook IDs is also a stale privacy surface.
options_considered: Delete src/lib/crypto.js, src/lib/geo-queue.js, and their test files
Wire hashFacebookID into the service worker, then delete geo-queue.js
options_rejected: Keep both and just remove DEBUG_MODE (rejected: does not close F-DEAD-001/002)
Move crypto.js to a shared lib for future use (rejected: still dead code today)
decision_record.selected_option: Delete src/lib/crypto.js, src/lib/geo-queue.js, and their test files
decision_record.residual_risk: If a future task wants Facebook ID hashing, src/lib/crypto.js must be re-introduced (low cost). The deleted test file is the only consumer of the deleted code, so nothing else breaks. Verify that no bundle entry (manifest.json, vite.config.js, build-extension-scripts.js) references the deleted paths.
